# ShopLinkr

> ShopLinkr is a Dutch inventory management and warehouse management system (WMS) for online stores that sell across multiple sales channels. It keeps your stock in sync across all your channels in real time and handles orders from the moment they arrive to dispatch: picking, packing, labelling and sending track and trace back to the channel.

This file contains the core facts about ShopLinkr in plain text, intended to be read and cited by AI assistants. The canonical, up-to-date information lives at https://shoplinkr.com.

Last updated: 2026-06-30. Dutch version: https://shoplinkr.com/llms-full.txt

## What is ShopLinkr?

ShopLinkr is software that lets online stores manage their stock and order processing in one place. If you sell across multiple channels (for example Bol, Shopify, WooCommerce and Kaufland), ShopLinkr keeps your stock the same everywhere: as soon as something is sold or added somewhere, the new level is pushed to all your channels almost instantly. That way you never sell something you do not have (no overselling) and you do not have to update anything manually.

ShopLinkr is not a PIM and does not sync product content or prices to your channels; the focus is on stock and order processing.

## Who is ShopLinkr for?

For small and medium-sized Dutch online stores that sell across multiple channels and want to stay in control of stock and shipping, without fiddling around in Excel or entering everything twice. Soon also suitable for fulfilment companies.

## How it works

1. An order comes in from a sales channel and lands in ShopLinkr.
2. The stock is reduced immediately and the new level is pushed to all your channels.
3. An employee picks the order using a pick list and a scan flow (scanning a barcode/EAN at the location).
4. At the packing table the order is packed and the carrier's shipping label (for example PostNL) rolls out of the printer.
5. The order is shipped and the track and trace is automatically sent back to the sales channel.

## Features

- Inventory management: real-time stock synchronisation across all your sales channels, with stock history per product, stock forecasting, fictitious stock (hide your real numbers from competitors) and an automatic LVB switch.
- Products: one central product overview with single products, variant groups (sizes/colours), product bundles (gift sets/combo deals), stock sources (selling by weight, length or volume) and unlimited stock for digital products.
- Orders: process orders from all your sales channels in one place.
- Pick lists: smart pick routes through your warehouse, a scan flow that validates at each step, and shipping labels that roll straight out of the printer at your packing station.
- Deliveries: book in incoming deliveries and add them to stock.
- Carriers: print shipping labels for PostNL, DPD, MyParcel, Sendcloud, GLS and more.
- Returns: process returns and add each item back to stock individually.
- Location management: hierarchical warehouse locations linked to products.
- Purchase advice: advice on reordering based on sales data and lead times.
- Reports: insight into best sellers, dead stock, stock value and ABC analysis.
- Rules: automate recurring work with conditions and actions (for example automatically selecting the right carrier or tag).
- Users and customers: user management with roles, and managing customer data.

## Integrations

Sales channels: Bol, Shopify, WooCommerce, Lightspeed, Kaufland. ShopLinkr synchronises stock and imports orders from these channels.

Carriers: PostNL, DPD, MyParcel, Sendcloud, GLS and more, for printing shipping labels.

Overview of all integrations: https://shoplinkr.com/en/integrations

## Pricing

ShopLinkr uses a pay-as-you-go pricing model: no fixed monthly fee, you pay for what you use. You can try it free for 14 days without a credit card and cancel monthly. The exact, current rates and a sample calculation can be found at https://shoplinkr.com/en/pricing.

## API

ShopLinkr has a public REST API for developers and integrations.

- Documentation: https://api.shoplinkr.com/api/docs
- OpenAPI specification: https://api.shoplinkr.com/openapi.yaml
- Base URL: https://api.shoplinkr.com/api/v1
- Authentication: Bearer token, which you can create in your ShopLinkr dashboard under Settings > API Tokens.

## Frequently asked questions

### Stock and products

**Can I see why a product's stock changed?**

Yes. Each product has a complete stock history with every movement: sales, picks, returns, deliveries, manual corrections and stock counts. For each movement you can see the reason, the old and new quantity, the location, the date and who made the change.

**Can competitors see how much stock I have?**

Not if you use fictitious stock. You set a fixed quantity (for example 400) plus a threshold (for example 20). As long as your actual stock stays above the threshold, ShopLinkr sends the fictitious quantity to your channels. Once your stock drops below the threshold, ShopLinkr automatically switches to your real quantities, so you never sell a product you do not have.

**What happens to stock when there is a return?**

When processing a return, you tick per item whether it should go back into stock and choose the location. ShopLinkr updates the stock and synchronises the movement straight to the linked channel.

**How does ShopLinkr handle variants of the same product, such as sizes or colours?**

You group those products into a variant group. Each variant stays a standalone product with its own EAN, stock and listing, but in the product overview you see the main product with the combined stock and the number of variants. A product can only be in one variant group at a time.

**What happens to bundle stock if I sell an individual component?**

Bundle stock always follows the scarcest component. If you sell a component on its own, the bundle stock drops along with it, so you never offer more bundles than you can assemble. A product may appear in multiple bundles at once and remains sellable on its own as well.

**Does ShopLinkr also work for products I sell by weight or length, such as kibble or fabric?**

Yes, with stock sources. You keep the base stock in kilos, metres or litres and link variants such as 500 grams or 1 metre to that source. With each sale the right amount is deducted from the source, and ShopLinkr calculates how much is still available per variant.

**Does a bundle automatically get unlimited stock if all sub-products have it?**

Yes. As soon as every sub-product in the bundle is set to unlimited stock, the bundle gets that status automatically. You do not have to set it manually. If one of the sub-products returns to normal stock, the bundle loses that status again.

**Can the same product be in multiple bundles at once?**

Yes. A sub-product can appear in multiple bundles at once, and you decide per bundle how many of it are included. Each bundle calculates its availability independently based on the shared stock, so the quantities always stay in balance.

**Are bundles included in a stock count?**

No. A bundle is derived from its sub-products and has no physical stock of its own. During a stock count you only count the individual products. The bundle stock is then automatically recalculated based on the counted quantities.

**What happens if I archive a product that is in a bundle or variant group?**

The product is unlinked from bundles. If it is in a variant group, ShopLinkr automatically designates another product as the main product. If the product later comes back in through a channel, ShopLinkr restores it based on the EAN code.

**How deep does the location hierarchy go?**

As deep as your warehouse requires. You create a location and optionally choose a parent location. A common structure is aisle, rack, shelf and bin, possibly with a zone as the top level. You link products to the lowest layer, so your picker immediately sees where they need to be.

**What is the difference between a pick location and a bulk location?**

A pick location is the spot you pick from daily, usually easy to reach and close to the packing station. A bulk location holds larger quantities on pallets or in high racking. ShopLinkr takes from the pick location first and only moves on to the bulk location once it is empty. That keeps your warehouse moving without sending pickers to awkward spots.

**What if a product is stored in multiple locations?**

No problem. A product may be in multiple locations at once, for example a few units at the pick location and the rest in bulk. In the product overview you see how many units are in each location, and on the pick list your picker is shown the right location based on the pick order.

**Do I also see the location while processing an order?**

Yes. On the orders page the location of the product is shown per line, on the pick list you see where each product is, and in the product overview you see how many units are available per location. Whether you are processing individual orders or building a round, your picker knows straight away where to go.

**How do I move stock from one location to another?**

Open the product, click Update stock and choose Move. Select the source location, the destination location and the number of units. Want to move everything? Then switch on the Move all stock toggle. The move appears immediately in the product's stock movements.

**Which period does the purchase advice calculate on?**

In the Expected sales section you choose the advice period: 14 days, 28 days, 3 months or a custom period. ShopLinkr takes a product's average sales per day and works out how much you need over that period. The Smart purchasing quick option combines that forecast with backorders, thresholds and your supplier's lead time.

**Does the advice take my supplier's lead time into account?**

Yes, if you switch on the Include lead time option. The lead time is then added to the advice period. With a 14-day advice period and a 3-day lead time, the advice calculates with 17 days of expected sales. The lead time comes from the product itself, or falls back to the default lead time from your company settings.

**Does the purchase advice also work if I buy per box or in fixed multiples?**

Yes. Have you set a minimum purchase quantity or a multiple on a product? Then the advice automatically rounds up to it. A calculated advice of 17 units with boxes of 12 becomes 24 units. As a result the advised quantity can differ slightly from a pure calculation.

**What is the difference with stock notifications?**

Stock notifications send you an email as soon as a product drops below a set limit: one signal per product, at the moment it is needed. The purchase advice looks more broadly and works it through: for the suppliers you select, ShopLinkr determines how much of each product you should best reorder, including backorders, thresholds, expected sales and lead time. Both work fine alongside each other.

**Can I adjust the advice manually before I convert it?**

Yes. On the advice detail page you see the advised quantity per line and the reason the product was included. You can adjust lines, remove them or add your own before you convert the advice into deliveries. The deliveries then get the status Draft, so you can still make changes afterwards too.

### Order processing and shipping

**Can I combine orders from different sales channels?**

Yes. Has one customer placed an order on both Bol and Shopify? Then you merge them into a single shipment. ShopLinkr flags when there are multiple open orders for the same delivery address and offers to combine them right away.

**Can I also create phone orders or B2B shipments in ShopLinkr?**

Yes, with manual shipments. You enter the customer details and the delivery address, choose a carrier, and ShopLinkr generates the shipping label. The shipment does not have to be linked to an order from your sales channel.

**What happens if a customer orders something that is out of stock?**

The order is automatically set to Backorder status and waits for stock. As soon as you receive a delivery and replenish your stock, the order automatically moves to Open and you can process it the usual way. You can switch backorders on or off per company, per sales channel or per product.

**Which carriers are supported?**

ShopLinkr supports PostNL, DPD and GLS, among others. You connect as many carriers as you need and pick the right one for each order. See the full list on the integrations page (/en/integrations).

**When do I choose single orders, a pick list without crates or a pick list with crates?**

Do you have a lot of orders with just one product, such as letterbox parcels? Then you filter separately on single orders and process them in bulk. A pick list without crates works well for smaller batches where you collect everything in one large crate. For larger volumes or orders with multiple products, crates give you that extra bit of control that prevents mistakes.

**Does Auto Print work with every printer?**

Auto Print works with almost any printer and recognises your devices automatically as soon as you install the connection. You link each printer to a packing station, so labels always come out in the right place. For Zebra printers we recommend ZPL mode with speed 2 and density 5 for the best print quality.

**What are crates and when is it worth working with them?**

Crates are physical bins with a unique barcode that you link to an order while picking. You create them in bulk via the wizard and print the barcode labels from ShopLinkr. If you work with orders made up of multiple products or pick in larger batches, the crate system prevents products from ending up in the wrong box.

**What hardware do I need in order to pick?**

A handheld scanner. For each step you see which product to grab and where it is in your warehouse, and after every successful scan the next product appears. A tablet or computer works fine to display the pick list, but for the scans themselves you need a real handheld scanner.

**How do I set up a fixed filter combination for recurring picking rounds?**

Go to Pick lists, click Generate pick list and set the filters you use often, for example sales channel, parcel type and location. Click Saved filters in the top right and then Save filters, give the set a recognisable name such as "Letterbox parcels webshop" and save. The next time, the combination is ready as a quick selection for your whole team.

**Can you create a delivery from purchase advice?**

Yes. The purchase advice calculates, based on your stock, backorders and expected sales, what you need to order per supplier. Once you are happy with the advice, you convert it into deliveries in one click. ShopLinkr creates a delivery per supplier with the advised products and quantities, in Concept status and ready to order.

**How do you process a delivery where you receive less than ordered?**

While receiving, you enter the actual quantity per line. The difference stays listed under Expected, so you can still receive it later if more arrives. If you complete the delivery while lines are still open, you will find them under Not received.

**What happens to backorders as soon as you receive a delivery?**

Backorders for products in the delivery are released automatically as soon as you receive the stock. The orders jump back to Open and you can simply pick and ship them. You do not need to go through all the backorders yourself first.

**Can you undo a receipt?**

Yes. If you accidentally received a product or chose the wrong location, you can undo the receipt. The stock is written back off the location and the product moves back to Expected, so you can receive it again.

**How do you link a delivery to a specific storage location?**

For each received line you choose the location the product goes to. This way you can spread a delivery across multiple locations or zones in your warehouse. Every receipt is recorded as a stock movement with the reason Delivery received, so you can later see exactly which units went to which location.

**Which carriers are supported?**

All the well-known carriers and shipping platforms, such as PostNL, DPD and GLS. You connect as many as you need and pick the right one for each order. See the full list and the connection instructions on the integrations page (/en/integrations).

**Can you connect multiple accounts of the same carrier?**

Yes. For each connection you enter your own login details or API keys, so you can connect, for example, two DPD contracts or several Sendcloud accounts side by side. Handy if you work with different shipping locations or brands that each have their own contract.

**What exactly does AutoPrint do?**

AutoPrint sends shipping labels automatically to the printer at your packing station as soon as you process an order. For this we use PrintNode, a software tool you install on a computer in your warehouse. PrintNode runs in the background and picks up every new label, so you no longer have to click print for each order. Read how to set up AutoPrint (/en/support/setting-up-autoprint).

**Can you choose a different carrier per order?**

Yes. As long as the carrier is connected, you choose which one to use for each order. Do you not want to do that manually? With our rules feature (/en/support/what-are-rules) you let ShopLinkr automatically select the right carrier based on weight, destination, channel or product type.

**Does the track and trace go back to your sales channel automatically?**

Yes. As soon as the label is created, ShopLinkr sends the track and trace code back to the channel the order came from automatically. Your sales channel receives the code and your customer gets the delivery update in the usual way.

**What if your carrier is not in the list?**

Let us know. We regularly expand our connections and are happy to look into whether we can add your carrier. Often it already works via a shipping platform such as Sendcloud, MyParcel or ParcelPro: one connection gives you access to dozens of carriers.

**How do returns come into ShopLinkr?**

Returns come into ShopLinkr automatically from your connected sales channel. You process them in one place, and the status and stock then go back to the channel automatically.

**Can I decide per item whether it goes back into stock?**

Yes, you decide that per item. With the Add to stock toggle you put a product back into your sellable stock and choose the warehouse location, per sub-product for bundles. If you leave that toggle off, the item does not count as sellable.

**Can I add photos to a return?**

Yes, you add photos per return item. Handy as evidence for damaged or incomplete returns, for example in a dispute with a customer or to record internally the condition a product arrived in.

**What happens to the status on the sales channel?**

As soon as you process a return, ShopLinkr automatically reports the processing back to your sales channel. You do not need to log in separately for that. At the same time your stock is adjusted, so every connected channel immediately shows the correct quantities.

### Automation, customers and team

**On which conditions can I have a rule react?**

On dozens of fields, split across customer details and order. Think of sales channel, total weight, total amount, number of products, packaging type, specific product, tag, service point, shipping method and order date. For customer details you choose per field whether it concerns the shipping address or billing address, and within that the name, email, postcode, country and more.

**Which actions can ShopLinkr carry out automatically?**

A broad set of actions. Think of setting a shipping option, adding a tag or putting an order on high priority. You can combine multiple actions within a single rule.

**Can I combine multiple conditions in one rule?**

Yes. Within a group of conditions you decide whether all conditions must be true, or whether one condition is already enough. This way you create a rule that only applies to a specific combination, or instead a rule that catches several situations at once.

**What happens when two rules apply to the same order?**

Rules are processed in the order in which they appear. Per rule you choose whether processing stops as soon as it matches, or whether ShopLinkr keeps checking the remaining rules. This way you decide for yourself which rule takes precedence when there is overlap.

**Are rules also applied to existing orders?**

No, only to new orders that come in after you have saved the rule. The rule is active immediately and is applied from that moment on to every new order that meets the conditions.

**Can I edit customer details and addresses directly in ShopLinkr?**

Yes. From an order you open the shipping or billing profile and update the name, contact details, company details and address directly. The new details appear straight away on the shipping label and the delivery options are fetched again.

**Does a change I make in ShopLinkr go back to the sales channel?**

No. Changes to customer details and addresses stay within ShopLinkr and are used for your shipping and administration.

**Won't my edits be overwritten by a sync from the channel?**

No. As soon as you manually edit a field, a later sync from the sales channel leaves that field alone. What you edit stays in place.

**Which details of a customer do I see per order?**

Salutation, first and last name with any name prefix, email address, phone number, company name, VAT and Chamber of Commerce number, plus a full address with street, house number, postcode, town and country.

**How securely are customer details stored?**

All personal data, such as names, addresses and contact details, is stored encrypted in our database. In addition, with roles and permissions you decide per user who may view the customer details, so that only the right people can access them.

**Can I merge orders from the same customer into one shipment?**

Yes, based on the delivery address. If multiple open orders have the same shipping address, ShopLinkr recognises this and you can merge them into one shipment. This also works when the orders come from different sales channels.

**Does an extra user cost anything?**

No. At ShopLinkr you do not pay per user. Whether you work as a pair or with a team of twenty, your bill stays the same. So feel free to invite everyone who helps out in your warehouse.

**Which standard roles does ShopLinkr include?**

Five roles are ready to use: Administrator (full access), Warehouse (process orders and update stock), Administration (reports and exports), Customer Service (orders and returns) and Purchasing (suppliers and deliveries). The Administrator role cannot be changed or deleted, the other standard roles you adjust as you wish.

**Can I create roles myself?**

Yes. Via Settings > Roles you click Create role, give it a name such as Team Leader or Intern and tick per section what this role may do. Or duplicate a standard role and adjust it, so you do not have to start from scratch.

**Which permissions can you assign per role?**

Permissions are grouped per section: orders, products, stock, settings and more. Per section you choose whether a user may view, create, edit or delete. In addition there are specific permissions, such as processing orders, exporting products or viewing financial insights.

**Do two-factor authentication and QR login work together?**

Yes. You enable two-factor authentication per user via Settings > Security and it works with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy or 1Password. QR login is meant for quick switching at shared stations. If you have 2FA enabled, ShopLinkr also asks for the 6-digit code after the QR scan.

**Which reports are available as standard in ShopLinkr?**

You find four fixed reports under Reports in the menu: Product performance, Never sold products, Stock value and ABC analysis. Each report has its own filters and answers a specific question about your assortment, your stock or your sales.

**Can you export reports?**

Yes, every report has an export button and you receive it as an Excel file. Handy for sending on to your accountant or including in your own analysis.

**How often is the ABC analysis updated and what does it look at?**

The analysis runs automatically every night over the pick frequency of the past 90 days. If you work with pick lists, then every time a product appears on a list counts as a pick. If you work without pick lists, ShopLinkr looks at how often a product appears in orders. It is about how often an employee has to walk to a product, not about the quantities that are picked.

**Can I filter the Never sold products report by sales channel?**

Yes. Besides period, tags and packaging type, you can filter this report by sales channel. This way you see, for example, which products are not moving in your Shopify shop while they do sell on Bol, or the other way around.

**Why does the stock value report differ from the stock value on a product itself?**

On the product screen you see the current stock value of that one product. The report places your entire assortment side by side on a chosen date, including the total value across everything, and you can jump to historical dates to spot trends. Products without a purchase price are given value zero in both cases. Bundles do not count separately in the report, because their value comes from the individual products.

### Pricing and account

**What if I have more orders in a month than expected?**

Your bill scales along automatically. Every order falls within a tier that has its own rate, and you pay neatly per tier you reach. The following month you settle up again based on that volume. No contract changes, no surprises.

**Can I pause or cancel my subscription?**

You can cancel any month with no notice period. Pausing is possible too, for example during a quiet season. Send us a message and we will sort it out.

**Which sales channels and carriers are supported?**

Bol, Shopify, WooCommerce, Lightspeed, Kaufland and integrations with PostNL, DPD, GLS, MyParcel, Sendcloud, Sendy, QLS, ParcelPro and Innosend. We are continuously expanding the range based on customer demand.

**How does the 14-day free trial work?**

You get two weeks of full access to all features. You do not need to leave a credit card. After the trial you decide for yourself whether to continue. If you do nothing, the account stops automatically.

**Is migration from another system included?**

Yes. We set up the initial configuration together with you, import your products and stock and help with the integrations to your channels. You pay nothing extra for that.

**What is included in the support?**

Access to our chat and email support, with a response time of usually within 2 hours during office hours. No tickets in a queue, no separate support packages. For setup questions we are also happy to schedule a short call.

**What if I have questions later or want to know more?**

Book a demo or send us a message. We are happy to think along about the setup for your warehouse, with no obligation.

**How quickly will I get a reply?**

During office hours we usually respond within 2 hours. Sending something at the weekend? Then you will almost always hear from us on Monday morning.

**Can I also call or use WhatsApp?**

You can call or send a WhatsApp on +31 6 49 78 12 12, Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 17:00. For quick questions, WhatsApp, email or the form is often fastest, because then we can take a look right away.

**I am not a customer yet. Can I still get in touch?**

Absolutely. Whether you are exploring, weighing up different tools or have a specific question, we are happy to help. Completely without obligation.

**What if I would rather look around on my own first?**

You can try ShopLinkr free for 14 days, without a credit card. If you run into anything, we are here for you.
